snapshot.legacyDesignToolsHead: b5dfb508 (origin/main at lane start; no legacy-design-tools commits made -- census is a read-only import of production resolver code, per the dispatch's own 'invent, add or change NO setback value')

prsAndDeploys: not applicable: doc_repo lane, no product-repo code changed, nothing merged or deployed. legacy-design-tools was read via a fresh lane/p225-setback-codification-census worktree branched from origin/main and never edited.
instrument: _inbox/2026-09-15_p225_census_instrument.mjs -- re-runnable: `npx tsx _inbox/2026-09-15_p225_census_instrument.mjs [--ldt-root <path>] [--out <path>]`; imports the REAL production getSetbackTableForZoning + mapDistrict from a legacy-design-tools worktree (no reimplementation of the match contract) and live-queries each wired city's public ArcGIS layer for a distinct-code parcel-count breakdown.
missionPremise: P-225 dispatch, live production finding 2026-09-15: an uncodified BDC district (GC/MU/PDD/...) 404s with no buildable envelope at all in Bastrop, root-caused in code (not inferred) to getSetbackTableForZoning routing every known BDC code to a table with only 4 rows, mapDistrict's first-token match then returning null for the rest, and resolveAuthoritativeSetbacks short-circuiting to null before the atom-chain candidate the resolver could otherwise use is ever built (authoritativeSetbackSource.ts:258-266). This lane censuses how widespread that gap-shape is across every onboarded jurisdiction; it does not fix it.
completionPredicate: A per-district codified/uncodified table for every live zoning district code in every wired city across the six onboarded counties, each uncodified district carrying one of the three named dispositions with a cited basis, a live parcel count per row, a total-parcels-dark count, and a re-runnable instrument. NOT FULLY MET: 2 of 18 in-scope city/county layer entries could not be live-queried (see contradicted + leave_behind) -- 16 of 18 were measured, covering 4 of 6 counties completely and a 5th (Travis) partially.
scopeBasis: Six onboarded counties = CONSTRAINT_SEARCH_COUNTIES (artifacts/api-server/src/lib/parcelConstraintSearch.ts:56-62): Bastrop 48021, Caldwell 48055, Hays 48209, McLennan 48309, Travis 48453, Williamson 48491 -- corroborated independently by scripts/p85/p85-clerk-portals.mjs's own six-county seed + 'all six counties permitted' operator note, and by two test/doc files naming Bexar and Bell as explicitly OUTSIDE the six-county serving ledger. New Braunfels (Comal), San Antonio (Bexar), Seguin + Cibolo (Guadalupe), and Killeen + Belton (Bell) all have live zoning layers and setback tables wired in this same repo but sit outside the six -- deliberately excluded from this census by county, not counted as uncodified districts. Full detail in CP1.
falsifier: Three falsifiers pre-registered in CP1 before any live derive call: (1) a sampled codified-district parcel must draw a live Polygon; (2) a sampled uncodified-district parcel must 404; (3) no county in the six should show zero uncodified districts without investigation. Results, run against https://smartsite.cloud's live buildable-envelope endpoint (the same PE proxy path scripts/surface-probe.mjs itself uses, no brokerage API key required): (1) PASS -- Bastrop SF-1 (codified) returned HTTP 200 status=ok with a real 7-vertex polygon on one of three freshly-sampled parcels (the other two returned the distinct, non-codification status no-buildable-area, a per-parcel geometry outcome, not a gap). (2) PASS -- Bastrop GC (uncodified) returned HTTP 404 {status:'no-district', reason:'No authoritative setback source covers this district — geometry not derived.'}, reproducing the dispatch's own cited string verbatim on an independently sampled parcel; Leander PUD-SF (uncodified) returned the same 404 twice. (3) TRIPPED as designed -- Caldwell returned zero rows and was investigated rather than accepted; traced to a dead Lockhart ArcGIS service URL, not a clean county.
contradicted: Two of the eighteen registered ZONING_LAYERS entries in the six-county scope could not be live-queried, contradicting the expectation (reasonable going in, given both carry 2026-07 'LIVE-VERIFIED' comments) that every registered layer URL still resolves: austin-tx's Publish_Zoning_AGOL/FeatureServer/0 now returns HTTP 499 'Token Required' even on a bare unauthenticated service-root request (a real access-gating change since the registry comment was written, not a malformed query -- confirmed with zero query parameters); lockhart-tx's Lockhart_City_Zoning_Online service is gone entirely -- listing every service under its ArcGIS org (kPfGI7KGlXn5IaHL) today returns only Parcels_with_CCAD_info and Road_Centerlines, no zoning service by any name. Also contradicted: Georgetown's own zoning-layers.ts:22 comment, which names 'RL' as one of 12 live-verified-covered setback districts (2026-07-20) -- the real georgetown-tx.json table carries no RL row today (RT and RM exist instead), and a live re-check confirms RL (3 parcels) is genuinely uncodified now, whatever the comment claims.

totalDistrictsCensused.rule: distinct canonical district codes (post codeDomainMap/codeExtractRegex/nullDistrictCodes normalization) with at least one live parcel, summed across the 16 successfully-queried city/county layer entries (18 registered in scope, 2 errored -- see contradicted)

codifiedDistricts.rule: of the 313, districts where getSetbackTableForZoning found a table AND mapDistrict returned kind matched or single (the real production resolver, not a reimplementation)

uncodifiedDistricts.rule: 313 - 141; getSetbackTableForZoning returned null, or the table had no districts, or mapDistrict returned null for the live code

uncodifiedParcels.rule: sum of live per-code parcel counts (server-side ArcGIS group-by-count, not client pagination) across the 172 uncodified rows -- the operator-facing 'how much of the product is dark' number. UNDERCOUNT: excludes Austin (Travis, largest city in scope, unmeasured) and Lockhart (Caldwell, unmeasured) entirely -- both cities' true uncodified-parcel contribution is unknown, not zero.

totalParcelsCensused.rule: sum of live per-code parcel counts across all 313 rows (codified + uncodified), same 16-of-18-layer caveat

dispositionAcquire.rule: of the 172 uncodified rows, a real codified ordinance plausibly exists but is untranscribed -- see instrument's KNOWN_DISPOSITIONS citations per row for the ~40 with direct per-city comment evidence; the remainder (flagged lowConfidenceDisposition:true in the census JSON) used a conservative default heuristic and are explicitly NOT verified per-code

dispositionRuledOutOfScope.rule: of the 172 uncodified rows, not a conventional Euclidean district (PUD/PDD composites, agricultural, overlay/form-based, repealed, or a not-a-district sentinel) -- includes Bastrop's 7 repealed B3 P-* codes and Leander's 9 individually-named PUD-project codes, both with direct live evidence, not a guess

dispositionServeFromAtomChain.rule: of the 172 uncodified rows, Bastrop's BDC conditional codes ONLY (MU/GC/PDD/PI/IND/OS) -- the one place this census found direct evidence (the dispatch's own live-read finding) of a usable atom-chain/GIS-layer-23 per-parcel value the resolver could reach if mapDistrict did not gate it out first. Not applied anywhere else: no equivalent evidence was independently verified for any other city's gap codes.

lowConfidenceDispositionRows.value: see census JSON rows where lowConfidenceDisposition is true
lowConfidenceDispositionRows.rule: any uncodified row with no direct per-city comment/doc citation, classified by a generic code-shape default heuristic (PUD/PDD/AG-prefix -> ruled-out-of-scope; a sentinel code -> ruled-out-of-scope; otherwise -> acquire) -- explicitly NOT a verified per-code research pass, named here so it is not mistaken for one

constraintsHonored: No setback value invented, added, or changed anywhere -- census only reads and imports the real getSetbackTableForZoning/mapDistrict from an unedited legacy-design-tools worktree.
No jurisdiction mapping edited (zoning-layers.ts, districtMapping.ts, setbacks/index.ts all read-only imports).

The resolver's gate order was not touched -- the fix this census's own finding points at (reordering resolveAuthoritativeSetbacks so the atom-chain candidate can be built even when mapDistrict fails) is explicitly named as a follow-on row's scope, not this one's.
No deploy attempted or needed -- nothing merged to legacy-design-tools.
No enumeration piped through tail; the full live JSON artifact is committed, not a truncated console sample.
Lane claimed before any file edit (node scripts/lane-claim.mjs claim, exit 0) and released at close.

Own fan only: two Explore/research passes were run as subagent calls that do not themselves spawn further subagents; verification of every subagent claim (the six-county list, the surface-probe.mjs location, the AGENTS.md warning) was re-done independently at source before being relied on, never taken on the subagent's word alone.
leave_behind: austin-tx's registered zoning layer URL (Publish_Zoning_AGOL/FeatureServer/0) now requires an ArcGIS token for even an unauthenticated metadata request -- a real access-gating change since the 2026-07-24 'LIVE-VERIFIED' registry comment, likely also breaking legacy-design-tools' own zoning-stamp.ts production job for Austin (not independently confirmed against the production job itself; flagged for someone who owns that pipeline to check). Austin is the single largest city in the six-county scope and is entirely unmeasured in this census as a result.

lockhart-tx's registered zoning layer URL (Lockhart_City_Zoning_Online) no longer exists under its ArcGIS org at all (confirmed via the org's own service listing) -- the registry entry is dead, not merely slow or token-gated. Caldwell county is entirely unmeasured in this census as a result. A follow-on task should either find Lockhart's current public zoning service or mark the registry entry explicitly stale.

Two documentation staleness findings, neither acted on here: legacy-design-tools/AGENTS.md:9-18 tells an agent to STOP if a task mentions Bastrop/municipal data, calling this 'the wrong repo' -- false today (getSetbackTableForZoning/SETBACK_TABLES/ZONING_LAYERS/buildable-envelope genuinely live here); and docs/property-explorer-setback-coverage-central-tx.md:29 (2026-07-23) describes a Bastrop routing policy ('every B3 P-* code resolves to bastrop-city-tx') that the current index.ts contradicts (repealed P-* codes now return null per WDLL STEP 3).

Georgetown's zoning-layers.ts:22 comment names 'RL' as one of 12 live-verified-covered districts; the current table has no RL row. Either the comment has a typo (RT/RM likely intended) or the row was removed since -- worth a two-minute human check, not chased further here.

scripts/surface-probe.mjs (doc_repo) carries no P-225 predicate and none was added -- this census produces a per-district table, not a per-parcel pass/fail row over a fixed parcel list, so the ontology does not map cleanly onto surface-probe.mjs's ROWS shape. P-225 sits in probe-close-gate.mjs's own PREDICATE_DEBT set (OPS24_RANGES [200,250]), so a close citing a parseable artifact (this one has zero P-225 rows, which is allowed) satisfies the mechanical gate; a future row that wants a standing customer-facing predicate for 'district X draws or honestly refuses' would need to design one, which is out of scope for a census.

131 of the 172 uncodified rows (5,095 parcels) carry a disposition from a generic code-shape default heuristic, not per-city ordinance research -- flagged lowConfidenceDisposition:true in the census JSON and should not be treated as individually verified. The acquire/ruled-out split on those rows is a reasonable first pass, not a researched call.
The census JSON (_inbox/2026-09-15_p225_census.json) is the committed artifact of record; this close's prose is a summary of it, not a substitute.
